name: The Black Iron Prison Vision
summary: PKD reports a recurring vision in which 1974 California is overlaid by 70 AD Rome — a vast iron prison housing the early Christians under imperial persecution. The vision continued at intervals through 1981.
During severe late-1970s depressive episodes, friends enlist Joan Simpson to help care for Dick, whose apartment is cluttered with papers, snuff cans, and medication bottles.
source_name: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Adds one of the requested women/relationships not yet represented in curated biography.

summary: At the 1977 Metz science-fiction convention in France, Dick publicly discloses 2-3-74 and describes it as a breakthrough to the real world behind appearances.
source_name: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Arnold notes that some friends feared the appearance signaled a downward spiral.

summary: Publishes A Scanner Darkly drawing on his drug culture experiences

Writes Julian Jaynes after reading The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, praising the theory and comparing Jaynes's divine-voice model to his own March 1974 right-hemisphere/Zagreus experience.
source_name: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Julian Jaynes, March 16, 1977
notes: Short quotations to foreground in display: "raving about it" and "Zagreus awaken in my right hemisphere." Letter id: LET_1977-03-16_JULIAN_JAYNES_0021.
entities: The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind

summary: Explains Jaynes's bicameral-mind theory to Mark Hurst and folds it into his developing VALIS/Zebra model of divine command voices.
source_name: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Mark Hurst, March 17, 1977

summary: Tells Carl Bennett that Jaynes's book provides scientific support for aspects of his Zebra speculation and right-hemisphere theory.
source_name: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Carl Bennett, March 30, 1977

summary: After several years without contact, PKD encounters William Sarill again and discusses how their theologies have changed since the Maze of Death period.
source_name: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Eugene Warren, July 28, 1977
notes: PKD writes that the encounter occurred the night before Warren's article arrived; he links Sarill to the theology in Maze and then describes his 1974 Trinitarian conversion.

name: Second 2-3-74 (Metz, 1977)
summary: Around the time of his Metz, France speech in September 1977, PKD reports a partial recurrence of the 2-3-74 phenomenology — pink-light states, AI Voice activity, and the Black Iron Prison overlay returning at intervals.

Writes Eugene Warren that Star Wars has religious importance because it makes Christian mystery available through popular science-fiction imagery, comparing Obi-Wan's voice to the voice he heard when VALIS took him over in March 1974.
source_name: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Eugene Warren, October 2, 1977
notes: Short quotations to foreground in display: "mystery of our religion" and "Word and Hand of God." Letter id: LET_1977-10-02_EUGENE_WARREN_0043.

summary: After returning from the Metz convention, writes Claudia Bush about the reception of his theology-heavy speech, a French romantic fixation, and seeing Star Wars.
source_name: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Claudia Bush, October 3, 1977

summary: Develops VALIS theology as systematic framework in the Exegesis notebooks
